nodes.description: Cytochrome c activates the apoptosome and downstream caspases. Biochemical studies of mature-protein G41S, Y48H and A51V report enhanced apoptosome activation. Thr20Ile instead reduces caspase-3/7 activity in engineered MEG-01 cells and lysates. This downstream readout does not directly establish defective apoptosome assembly for Thr20Ile. The effect on platelet production is still a hypothesis.

nodes.description: Pathogenic cytochrome c substitutions alter local stability and conformational dynamics without necessarily disrupting the overall fold. Human G41S, Y48H and A51V show greater conformational flexibility associated with enhanced apoptosome activation. G41S does not produce the same mobility change in the mouse protein. Mature-protein G41S, Y48H and A51V correspond to initiator-inclusive Gly42Ser, Tyr49His and Ala52Val.

nodes.description: Cytochrome c transfers electrons in the mitochondrial respiratory chain. G41S/Y48H models and Lys101del yeast show reduced respiratory function; by contrast, a Thr20Ile knock-in MEG-01 clone shows increased basal and maximal respiration. Cellular oxygen consumption measures the integrated respiratory phenotype and does not isolate the electron-transfer rate of each mutant protein. Respiratory abnormalities have not been established as a sufficient cause of thrombocytopenia.

nodes.description: In the G41S Cargeeg family, extravascular marrow contains platelet-like structures lacking the normal marginal microtubule coil. Premature release outside marrow vessels is proposed to reduce effective circulating platelet output. Patient-derived megakaryocytes can nevertheless form proplatelets normally in culture, implicating marrow context. These observations are not a proven universal mechanism for every CYCS allele.
